message:
test(apk): an IDR lost while the decoder was not ready comes back once it is; a test-build progress trace of the session (keepalive-r2 e, Codex apk-decoder-liveness r2)

Codex r2: (b) -- no receive / control dependence on a slow codec -- is 27d5966. (a) -- the current IDR
queued and shown once the decoder is ready -- is to be measured before anything is changed, and the
two unexplained intervals of ke-r23 need a trace on the next AVD run.

Axis 2 (android_decoder_idr_recovery_test): the PRODUCT shared session -- its control loop with the
owed-key retry (8 x 1 s) and the limiter, its UDP receive loop, control over the video socket as on
the relay path -- into the APK sink, a fake host on loopback (its own UdpControlChannel, product
timings; RequestKeyFrame answered with an IDR of the current generation). The selection's IDR comes
before the decoder is ready; ready comes 12 s later (beyond the 8 asks): U1 no surface, U2 the
codec's create held, U4 no surface then a held create, U3 a newer selection meanwhile; each with a
host that keeps sending deltas and an idle one. Judged from ready: the current IDR is the codec's
first input, a picture of it is presented, control stays open, and the client's keepalive keeps
reaching the host while the decoder is not ready.
- 27d5966 + this: 36/36. The owed budget IS spent before ready (U1 8 asks, U4 idle 10), and the
  recovery comes from what is already there: U1 the surface's re-arm (a new token: asked +5 ms),
  U2 / U4 the IDR kept by the worker / inbox (queued +2 ms). No policy change made for (a).
- 9f9a91c sink: 6 FAIL -- the keepalive silent 12-30 s at the host while the codec is held (the
  receive loop AND the control thread wait on the sink), and U3 queues the superseded generation's IDR.
- mutant m3 (no re-arm when the surface comes): 2 FAIL (U1 idle never recovers: the budget is gone).

Trace (client_liveness_trace.hpp; recorded only with GNLINK_LIVENESS_TRACE -- the APK's
-Pgnlink.livenessTrace=true, debug only, refused for a release; native marker "liveness-trace" added
to the release gate's APK_NATIVE_TEST_MARKERS): what the receive thread and the control thread are
doing and since when (phase, tid), the last datagram / control packet / tick, the longest sink
delivery, the owed token / attempts / next ask, the limiter's taken / refused wants, the last keyframe
request written (its seq -- the Host logs the same `keyframe-request seq=` -- reason, result, the
transport message count), the UDP control channel's counters and close reason; the decoder worker's
last pass, the codec call it is in (mu_ released) and its tid. Relaxed atomics only on the receive
path: no lock, no I/O. The app logs it as `liveness_trace` twice a second from a thread of its own
(nativeLivenessTrace). Without the flag nothing is recorded and the call returns ""; the Kotlin
logger is behind BuildConfig.LIVENESS_TRACE (false in every shipped build).
APK: plain debug / release (no marker), trace debug (marker in all 4 .so), release with the flag:
refused. Windows: the decoder tests 6/6, client_udp_recv_loop, prelogin 60/60, xbutton 75/75,
role_park 13/13, shared_core -- all exit 0.
